error_codes.meaning: The request cannot succeed as written: a field is missing or malformed, or the body is not what the endpoint takes. details.reason names the class.
The Agent source still has empty required slots; fill them before building or publishing.
A session policy document does not satisfy the policy schema.
The session policy refused this input.
No access token was sent, or the kernel did not accept it.
The token is valid but lacks the scope this operation needs.
The named resource or endpoint does not exist.
The expected revision or command identity no longer matches; read the current state, then decide again.
The runtime state conflicts with this request.
The session is closed; reopen it first.
The session is archived; unarchive it first.
The session has unfinished or queued work; try again when it settles.
The kernel is momentarily at capacity; retry later with the same ids.
The kernel or its store cannot serve the request now; a retry with the same ids is safe.
The write may or may not have happened. Inspect it by its original ids before retrying; never resend under a new id.
The input was rejected locally, before reaching the kernel.
A local file could not be read or written.
The kernel speaks a protocol or response shape this client does not.
The kernel or this client does not offer the operation.
The kernel answered with an HTTP failure that carries no recognizable error body.
The command was interrupted.

notes: CLI and inbound MCP share the Rust operation engine and contract schemas. See docs/verification/agent-development-cli-mcp.md for actual acceptance scope.
Resource-bearing native deployment actions can require additional resources permission at the kernel; source edits only save data.
NativeJson fields preserve original DTO JSON text; explicit refs preserve native control integers in decimal strings within the native u64 range.
Managed source projects accept incomplete Agents and use the same pure editing engine as local CLI files.
SessionPolicy, Agent v2 and nofy.session-control/v1 are implemented; the frontend is not included.
CAS means local compare-before-update, not a commercial product or external authentication service.
Module repositories store immutable source packages; Agent declarations retain pinned imports and bindings. Export includes referenced source bytes without installing external dependencies.
